key: But will God in very truth dwell on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded!
s: Dedicating the Temple, Solomon turns in his prayer to what the house can be; Radak, on 8:27, reads a house built for God as a figure, since no place contains Him, and Solomon as asking that the chosen place aid prayer like an interceding angel.

evidence.gloss: That is: is it true that God dwells with man on earth? That cannot be believed, for You are exalted above all, no place contains You, You are the place of the world and the world is not Your place; so my building the house for You is only by way of figure, that Your will and glory be found in this house to hear the prayer prayed in this place; and though His will in every place is toward whoever cries to Him with a whole heart, Solomon asked God that this chosen place help the one who prays, as though the house were an interceding angel, and that prayer here be heard more nearly than in another place.

Both faults hold in the standing sentence: ‘built so that prayer ...’ dangles after ‘God’, and Radak says the building of the house FOR God is only by way of figure (מה שבניתי הבית לך אינו אלא על דרך משל), not that the house is a figure, while the interceding-angel clause is Solomon’s request (בקש שלמה מהאל שיהיה המקום הזה הנבחר מסייע המתפלל בתפלתו כאילו הבית הזה היה מלאך מליץ), not a purpose in Radak’s own voice. Corrected to the refuter’s sentence: a house built for God read as a figure, since no place contains Him (אין לך מקום שיכילך), and Solomon as asking that the chosen place aid prayer like an interceding angel; every clause is in the evidence.
